about: The Te Deum is an ancient hymn of praise and thanksgiving. In it the Church confesses the majesty of the Holy Trinity, addresses Christ as King of glory and Judge, and then asks for salvation, protection and mercy. This edition retains the full traditional Roman text through its final act of trust.

seg.tr: We praise Thee, O God; we acknowledge Thee to be the Lord.

ex.w006: In the hymn the verb means publicly to confess and acknowledge God as Lord.

seg.tr: Thee, the Father everlasting, all the earth doth worship.

a.g: All the earth worships You, the everlasting Father

seg.tr: To Thee all Angels; to Thee the heavens and all the Powers:
to Thee the Cherubim and Seraphim continually cry:

ex.w027: The Cherubim and Seraphim continually take up the threefold “Holy.”

seg.tr: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth.
Heaven and earth are full of the majesty of Thy glory.

a.g: The heavens and the earth are full

seg.tr: Thee, the glorious choir of the Apostles; Thee, the admirable company of the Prophets,

a.g: The glorious choir of apostles praises You
the admirable company of prophets praises You

seg.tr: Thee, the white-robed army of the Martyrs, doth praise.

a.g: the white-robed army of martyrs praises You

ex.w052: The adjective presents the martyrs as an army clothed in the white robes of victory.

seg.tr: Thee throughout the world
the holy Church doth acknowledge:
the Father of infinite majesty; Thy adorable, true and only Son;

a.g: Your true and only Son, worthy of reverence

seg.tr: also the Holy Ghost, the Comforter. Thou, O Christ, art the King of glory.

a.g: also the Holy Spirit, the Comforter

ex.w078: From this point the hymn addresses Christ directly.

seg.tr: Thou art the everlasting Son of the Father. When Thou didst take upon Thee to deliver man,

a.g: You are the Father’s everlasting Son
intending to assume human nature for deliverance

ex.w087: Christ’s intention to assume human nature looks ahead from the moment described by horruísti.
ex.w088: The eternal Son named just before this clause assumes humanity in the Incarnation.

nt.w086: As a gerund after ad, liberándum expresses the purpose of deliverance, with its human object understood, while hóminem belongs to susceptúrus. It can alternatively be a gerundive agreeing with hóminem, humanity to be freed. In that reading the object of susceptúrus is understood.

seg.tr: Thou didst not disdain the Virgin’s womb.

ex.w090: The clause denies recoil from the Virgin’s womb through fear or aversion.

seg.tr: Having overcome the sting of death,
Thou didst open the kingdom of heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, in the glory of the Father.

a.g: You sit at God’s right hand

seg.tr: We believe that Thou shalt come to be our Judge.

a.g: We believe that You will come as judge

ex.w112: The Latin addresses Christ in a passive construction. The caption recasts it actively as the praying community’s confession: “We believe.”

seg.tr: We therefore pray Thee to help Thy servants,
whom Thou hast redeemed with Thy Precious Blood.

a.g: whom You have redeemed with precious blood

seg.tr: Make them to be numbered with Thy Saints in glory everlasting.

a.g: Have us numbered with Your saints in eternal glory

ex.w130: The prayer asks that God’s servants be numbered among the saints in everlasting glory.

seg.tr: Save Thy people, O Lord, and bless Thy inheritance.
Govern them, and raise them up for ever.
Every day we bless Thee.
and we praise Thy name for ever, yea, for ever and ever.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, this day to keep us without sin.

a.g: to keep us free from sin this day

seg.tr: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us. Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in Thee.

a.g: May Your mercy, Lord, be upon us

seg.tr: In Thee, O Lord, have I hoped; I shall not be confounded for ever.

a.g: may I never be put to shame

ex.w194: The closing act of trust asks that hope placed in the Lord may never end in shame.
